properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Alex's idea (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-11; his input is ADVISORY per rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word.

HIS WORDS: "You should put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph or something. And put the skill in your skills. That way you get what you want."

TWO HALVES, AND ONE IS ALREADY DONE. The skill half is satisfied: `report-friction` is served and ships in the kit, one of eighteen — that he asked for it is itself recorded as evidence under fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11, because a user asking for an installed capability is the sharpest form of `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`. THE NEW HALF IS CONSENT: nothing in reflow2 asks whether a project is willing to send anything back, and nothing records the answer. Grepped 2026-08-11 — no consent, opt-in-to-feedback or telemetry machinery exists anywhere in the core or the surface.

⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT COLLECTION. Every piece of field evidence reflow2 has was carried back by hand, by two people who happen to talk to each other. dec:idea-field-evidence-is-a-prioritisation-input asks whether that evidence should reach prioritisation; this asks whether the evidence ARRIVES AT ALL from anyone outside that circle. A prioritisation input with a single-digit number of sources is not a prioritisation input, and weighting by SOURCE INDEPENDENCE — the honest version of that idea — is impossible while every source is the same two households.

⭐⭐ AND ALEX'S FRAMING IS THE DESIGN, not a nicety. "ASKS ME... AND STORE MY DECISION IN THE GRAPH." Not a config flag, not an env var, not a default: a decision, asked once, on the record, revisitable. That is `cap:governance-proposal`'s shape applied to the consumer relationship rather than to a build rule, and it is exactly what `req:defaults-do-not-assert` demands of anything with a substantive default — silence must not read as yes, and it must not read as no either.

WHERE IT WOULD LIVE. `req:frictionless-update` is accepted ("install is one command, update is one word", modelled on Claude Code). The update path is the natural moment to ask: it already exists, it is already a place a human is present and consenting to something, and `reflow2 update` is queued work. Asking at INSTALL rather than UPDATE was considered and reads worse — at install nobody has used the tool yet, so there is nothing to have an opinion about.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A one-time ask at update, recorded as a Decision in the graph with the user's word. Revisitable, visible in the design, and it costs nothing when declined.
(b) Ask, but record it OUTSIDE the graph (a config file). Keeps the design clean of tooling state and loses the thing Alex specifically asked for — a decision he can see and change later.
(c) No ask. Keep `report-friction` as the only route and make it more discoverable instead. Cheapest and it does nothing about arrival rate.
(d) Ask, and additionally make the reporting one command. Alex's whole framing is "that way you get what you want", which reads as him volunteering — the bottleneck he is naming is that nobody asked him, not that he lacked a tool.

⚠️⚠️ THE HOLE THIS LANDS ON IS ALREADY NAMED AND STILL OPEN. `docs/partnership.md` lists DATA-PRIVACY MARKING among the three uncovered failure modes: "local-first by decision, and report-friction redacts by design; but NO FIELD IS MARKED SENSITIVE, so nothing can enforce redaction mechanically." A consented feedback channel makes that hole load-bearing. Consent to send is not consent to send ANYTHING, and today the redaction is a skill's discipline rather than a property the graph can check. This must not ship ahead of that.

⚠️ SECOND: consent recorded in a design that gets EXPORTED and committed is consent that travels. Whose consent is it when a second contributor pulls the repo? `req:a-node-can-say-who-may-change-it` (proposed) is the adjacent unbuilt piece, and this is a concrete case for it.

⚠️ THIRD, and it cuts against the whole idea: reflow2 is local-first by decision (`dec:repo-file-embedded` weighs "the user's design on a machine they do not control" AGAINST a service). Any channel that sends anything anywhere is in tension with that, and the honest version may be a channel that only ever produces a FILE the user chooses to send — which is what report-friction already does.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 ask, once, whether a project wants to send feedback back, and record that consent in the graph?
properties.rationale: Every piece of field evidence reflow2 holds arrived by hand from two related sources, which is precisely why the prioritisation idea recorded beside it cannot weight by source independence. Alex's framing — ask once, record the decision in the graph — is the right shape and matches how this project already handles a rule's consequence. The blocker is that it lands squarely on the data-privacy-marking hole partnership.md names as uncovered, where redaction is a skill's discipline rather than anything the graph can enforce.
